problem: The company wanted to test whether shorter weeks could improve work-life balance without hurting output.
title: Microsoft Japan trials a four-day work week
context: Microsoft Japan ran a pilot called the Work Life Choice Challenge with about 2,300 employees.
decision_made: Close offices every Friday in August 2019 and give employees the day off.
action_taken: Also limited meetings to 30 minutes and encouraged remote communication.
observed_outcome: Sales per employee rose almost 40 percent versus August 2018; 92 percent of employees were happy with the four-day week.
lessons: A short trial with other efficiency changes can show gains, but the result may not be a clean effect of the shorter week.
limitations: One month only, sales per employee is a narrow metric, other changes ran at the same time, managers reported pushback and results varied by department.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft Japan closed offices on Fridays in August 2019 as a trial.
Sales per employee rose by almost 40 percent compared with August 2018.
